subject.title: [Feature]: Option to force-prepend an opening <think> tag for local reasoning models

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class default-off synthetic `<think>` opener option, or should delimiter behavior stay provider-owned through existing params and model metadata?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but this would add a new output-format/config contract in an area where VISION.md and AGENTS.md ask for lean core and careful config-surface ownership.

options.title: Prefer provider-owned controls first
options.body: Use existing provider params and model metadata for model-specific thinking behavior, and add a core delimiter option only if maintainers confirm those seams cannot cover the observed models.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow core option
options.body: Add one documented default-off config path, wire it through runner and subscriber params, and prove streaming plus final-message behavior with native-tag and no-tag cases.

options.title: Close as not planned
options.body: Reject frontend-side delimiter synthesis and ask users to rely on provider request settings, prompt templates, or model-specific config instead.

recommendation.title: Prefer provider-owned controls first
recommendation.body: Use existing provider params and model metadata for model-specific thinking behavior, and add a core delimiter option only if maintainers confirm those seams cannot cover the observed models.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior maintainer review, current config history, and adjacent embedded-agent reasoning work point to steipete as the best owner for the product-boundary decision.
